processing: Details for this garden are not documented; as usual for Darjeeling, the leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, lightly in spring.
harvest_season: First flush lots are on the market, including the 2025 harvest; other flushes follow the usual Darjeeling calendar.
appearance_dry: Not specifically described; typical of Darjeeling first flush, expect wiry leaf in mixed green and brown.
appearance_liquor: Not specifically described; Darjeeling first flush usually gives a pale gold cup.
appearance_wet: Typically a mix of green and lightly coppered leaf for a spring Darjeeling.
taste_profile: One taster of a 2025 first flush found it light and pleasant, with an earthy aroma and a slight peppery bite at the end. Evidence beyond that is thin.

brewing.notes: Western style, gently as with other first flush Darjeeling. Longer or hotter brews bring out the bite.

vintage_note: Seen sold as a dated first flush, for example from the 2025 harvest. As with other spring Darjeeling, buy the current year and drink within about a year. Little is known about its other flushes on the market.
description:
Mission Hill is a tea estate in the hills of the Kalimpong subdivision, included among Darjeeling's gardens. It lies east of Lower Fagu, near the Fagu to Mission Hill road. It is one of the less documented names on the list.

No account of its factory methods is readily available. As with other Darjeeling first flush, expect light oxidation and a fresh, sharp character.

One reviewer of the 2025 first flush described a light, pleasant cup with a peppery finish and thought it worked with milk or with lemon and sugar, though not worth a price premium over an average Darjeeling. That is one opinion, but it is a fair prompt to taste before buying much.

Buy small and check the harvest year. For comparison, drink it next to a first flush from a better-known garden.
history: Little is documented about when the estate was founded or who has owned it. It appears in a Darjeeling tea declaration among estates of the Kalimpong hills, and it was still selling a dated first flush from the 2025 harvest.
